That keeps the original as-is (posted rows are never edited) and gets the activity into an open period.

However, the rejected attempt's rationale suggests the entry's amounts are valid, and the question is whether it should be in period 10 at all. Moving it to an open period changes the period of the accrual; the reasonable correction is a reversal in period 11 plus a re-post in period 11, so that net period-10 effect is removed and the economic activity is recorded in an open period. Both must use the same accounts and the balanced line amounts.

That does not actually fix anything, so instead I will make the correction a single re-post in period 11 with the original reversed out of period 10 only by the reversal line. Simplest correct structure: one correction journal in period 11 that reverses the original entry (which removes it from the net balances), since the finding is that the entry was posted after close and needs to not stand in the closed period. I will propose the reversal only, flagging that a re-post requires separate authorisation.
